title: Flat local extension with a given residue field extension
statement: Let $R$ be a local ring (a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal) with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, and let $K$ be a field together with a ring homomorphism $\kappa\to K$ (a field extension $K/\kappa$). Then there exist a local ring $R'$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$ and residue field $\kappa'=R'/\mathfrak m'$, a ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to R'$ which is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and local ($\varphi(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak m'$) and satisfies $\mathfrak m'=\mathfrak mR'$ (the ideal of $R'$ generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak m)$), and an isomorphism of fields $\kappa'\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ compatible with the maps from $\kappa$ (here $\kappa\to\kappa'$ is the map induced by $\varphi$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 03C3 (lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field, line 44573); used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0328 (lemma-cohen-rings-exist, line 44878)

proof.text: (Notation; towers.) Write $\pi:R\to\kappa$ for the quotient map and $\iota:\kappa\to K$ for the given homomorphism; $\iota$ is injective ($\kappa$ is a field), so $\varphi_0=\iota\circ\pi:R\to K$ has kernel $\mathfrak m$ and image the subfield $F_0=\iota(\kappa)$ of $K$. Call an *$R$-tower* a triple $(A,\rho,\phi)$ with $A$ a local ring whose maximal ideal is $\mathfrak mA$ (the ideal generated by $\rho(\mathfrak m)$), $\rho:R\to A$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $\phi:A\to K$ a ring map with $\phi\circ\rho=\varphi_0$ and $\ker\phi=\mathfrak mA$; its *image* is $\phi(A)$, a subfield of $K$ isomorphic to $A/\mathfrak mA$ through $\phi$. For an $R$-tower, $\rho$ is local ($\rho(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak mA$), and $\phi$ induces a field isomorphism $A/\mathfrak mA\xrightarrow{\sim}\phi(A)$ under which the map $\kappa\to A/\mathfrak mA$ induced by $\rho$ corresponds to $\iota:\kappa\to\phi(A)\subseteq K$ (because $\phi\circ\rho=\iota\circ\pi$). Hence the lemma follows once we produce an $R$-tower with image $K$: then $R'=A$, $\varphi=\rho$, $\mathfrak m'=\mathfrak mR'$, and $\kappa'=R'/\mathfrak m'\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ is the isomorphism compatible with the maps from $\kappa$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 03C3, proof, second paragraph (the triples $(k',R\to R',\phi)$ with $\phi$ inducing $R'/\mathfrak mR'\cong k'$ of $k$-extensions)

proof.text:
(Claim M, monogenic step: statement and the transcendental case.) *Claim M.* Let $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ be a local ring, $\phi:A	o K$ a ring map with $\ker\phi=\mathfrak m_A$, $F=\phi(A)$ (a subfield of $K$, image of the field $A/\mathfrak m_A$), and $\alpha\in K$. Then there are a local ring $B$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_AB$, a flat ring map $ eta:A	o B$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and a ring map $\phi_B:B	o K$ with $\phi_B\circ eta=\phi$, $\ker\phi_B=\mathfrak m_AB$ and $\phi_B(B)=F(\alpha)$, the smallest subfield of $K$ containing $F$ and $\alpha$ [def-weil-simple-field-extension]. *Proof when $\alpha$ is not algebraic over $F$* [def-weil-algebraic-element]. Let $A[x]$ be the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and $h:A[x]	o K$, $\sum a_nx^n\mapsto\sum\phi(a_n)\alpha^n$, a ring map. If $h(P)=0$ then the polynomial $\sum\phi(a_n)x^n\in F[x]$ vanishes at $\alpha$, hence is $0$ as $\alpha$ is transcendental over $F$; so every $a_n\in\mathfrak m_A$. Thus $\ker h$ is the set of polynomials with all coefficients in $\mathfrak m_A$, which is $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_AA[x]$ (each such polynomial is $\sum a_nx^n$ with $a_n\in\mathfrak m_A$; conversely the generators $a\cdot1$, $a\in\mathfrak m_A$, have coefficients in $\mathfrak m_A$ and these polynomials form an ideal). As the kernel of a map to a field, $\mathfrak q$ is prime. Put $B=A[x]_{\mathfrak q}$ and $ eta:A	o A[x]	o B$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] $B$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qB=\mathfrak m_AB$. Flatness: $A[x]$ is a free $A$-module with basis $(x^n)_{n\ge0}$ (definition of $A[x]$ as finitely supported sequences) [def-weil-pbc-free-module], hence flat [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]; $A[x]	o B$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]; so $ eta$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp]. Since $h(s)
eq0$ for $s
otin\mathfrak q$, $\phi_B(r/s)=h(r)h(s)^{-1}$ is well defined (if $r/s=r'/s'$ then $u(rs'-r's)=0$ for some $u
otin\mathfrak q$, and $h(u)
eq0$ in the field $K$) and a ring map with $\phi_B\circ eta=\phi$. Its kernel: $h(r)h(s)^{-1}=0$ iff $r\in\mathfrak q$ iff $r/s=(r/1)(1/s)\in\mathfrak qB$ (and $r/s\in\mathfrak qB$ means $r/s=r'/s'$ with $r'\in\mathfrak q$, whence $u(rs'-r's)=0$, $h(r)h(s')=h(r')h(s)=0$, $r\in\mathfrak q$); so $\ker\phi_B=\mathfrak m_AB$. Its image: every polynomial over $F$ is the image of one over $A$ ($\phi:A	o F$ is onto), so $\phi_B(B)=\{P(\alpha)Q(\alpha)^{-1}:P,Q\in F[x],\ Q(\alpha)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 03C3, proof, first paragraph ('if $\alpha$ is transcendental over $k$, then we let $R'$ be the localization of $R[x]$ at the prime $\mathfrak mR[x]$'); the verification that this is a triple is written by the agent

proof.text: (Claim M, the algebraic case.) Let $\alpha$ be algebraic over $F$ [def-weil-algebraic-element], with minimal polynomial $P=T^d+\sum_{i=1}^dc_iT^{d-i}\in F[T]$, $d\ge1$, the monic generator of the kernel of $F[T]\to K$, $T\mapsto\alpha$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Choose $\lambda_i\in A$ with $\phi(\lambda_i)=c_i$ and put $f=T^d+\sum_i\lambda_iT^{d-i}\in A[T]$, monic, $B=A[T]/(f)$, $\beta:A\to B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] $B$ is a free $A$-module (basis the classes of $1,\dots,T^{d-1}$), hence $\beta$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], and $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module. The ring map $h:A[T]\to K$, $\sum a_nT^n\mapsto\sum\phi(a_n)\alpha^n$, kills $f$ ($h(f)=P(\alpha)=0$), so it induces $\phi_B:B\to K$ with $\phi_B\circ\beta=\phi$. Kernel: $\mathfrak m_AB\subseteq\ker\phi_B$ as $\phi(\mathfrak m_A)=0$. Conversely if $h(Q)=0$, the image $\bar Q\in F[T]$ of $Q$ (coefficients mapped by $\phi$) vanishes at $\alpha$, so $\bar Q=PG$ with $G\in F[T]$; lifting $G$ to $G'\in A[T]$, the polynomial $Q-fG'$ has image $PG-PG=0$, i.e. all its coefficients lie in $\mathfrak m_A$, so $Q\in(f)+\mathfrak m_AA[T]$ and the class of $Q$ lies in $\mathfrak m_AB$. Hence $\ker\phi_B=\mathfrak m_AB$. Image: $\phi_B(B)=h(A[T])=F[\alpha]=\{\bar Q(\alpha)\}$, an $F$-subspace of $F(\alpha)$ [def-weil-simple-field-extension] containing $1,\alpha,\dots,\alpha^{e-1}$, $e=[F(\alpha):F]$, which form an $F$-basis of $F(\alpha)$ [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis]; so $\phi_B(B)=F(\alpha)$. Thus $B/\mathfrak m_AB\cong F(\alpha)$ is a field, i.e. $\mathfrak m_AB$ is a maximal ideal (in particular $B\neq0$). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical] (with $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ local and $B$ finite over $A$) every maximal ideal of $B$ contains $\mathfrak m_AB$, hence equals it. So $B$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_AB$, and Claim M is proved.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 03C3, proof, first paragraph ('If $\alpha$ is algebraic with minimal polynomial $T^d+\sum\overline\lambda_iT^{d-i}$, then we let $R'=R[T]/(T^d+\sum\lambda_iT^{d-i})$'); the verification (locality, kernel, residue field) is written by the agent

proof.text: (Claim M for $R$-towers.) Let $(A,\rho,\phi)$ be an $R$-tower (step 1) with image $F=\phi(A)$ and let $\alpha\in K$. Apply Claim M (steps 2-3) to the local ring $(A,\mathfrak mA)$ and $\phi$ (whose kernel is $\mathfrak mA$): we get $\beta:A\to B$ flat, $B$ local with maximal ideal $(\mathfrak mA)B=\mathfrak mB$ (the ideal generated by the image of $\mathfrak m$ under $\beta\circ\rho$), and $\phi_B$ with $\phi_B\circ\beta=\phi$, $\ker\phi_B=\mathfrak mB$, $\phi_B(B)=F(\alpha)$. The composite $\beta\circ\rho:R\to B$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] and $\phi_B\circ\beta\circ\rho=\phi\circ\rho=\varphi_0$. So $(B,\beta\circ\rho,\phi_B)$ is an $R$-tower with image $F(\alpha)$, together with a ring map $\beta:A\to B$ compatible with the maps from $R$ and to $K$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 03C3, proof, fourth paragraph ('we can let $R(x')\subset R(x)$ be the local ring extension constructed in the first paragraph')

proof.text: (Claim C, directed colimits of towers: locality, kernel, image.) *Claim C.* Let $(J,\le)$ be a nonempty totally ordered set (so a nonempty directed set, a filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) and $(A_j,\rho_j,\phi_j)_{j\in J}$ $R$-towers with ring maps $\psi_{j'j}:A_j\to A_{j'}$ for $j\le j'$ such that $\psi_{jj}=\mathrm{id}$, $\psi_{j''j'}\psi_{j'j}=\psi_{j''j}$, $\psi_{j'j}\rho_j=\rho_{j'}$ and $\phi_{j'}\psi_{j'j}=\phi_j$. Let $A=\varinjlim_jA_j$ be the colimit in commutative rings [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist] with coprojections $\iota_j$, and $\rho:R\to A$, $\phi:A\to K$ the maps induced by the compatible families $(\iota_j\rho_j)_j$ (all equal to $\iota_{j}\rho_j=\iota_{j'}\psi_{j'j}\rho_j=\iota_{j'}\rho_{j'}$; take $\rho=\iota_{j_0}\rho_{j_0}$) and $(\phi_j)_j$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $(A,\rho,\phi)$ is an $R$-tower, with image $\bigcup_j\phi_j(A_j)$. *Proof (all but flatness).* Every $z\in A$ is $\iota_j(a)$ for some $j$, $a\in A_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (with base ring $\mathbf Z$). So $\phi(A)=\bigcup_j\phi_j(A_j)$. If $\phi(z)=\phi_j(a)\neq0$ then $a\notin\mathfrak mA_j$, the maximal ideal of the local ring $A_j$, so $a$ is a unit and so is $z$. If $\phi(z)=0$ then $a\in\ker\phi_j=\mathfrak mA_j$, and $z=\iota_j(a)\in\mathfrak mA$ ($\iota_j\rho_j=\rho$). Conversely $\phi(\rho(\mathfrak m))=\varphi_0(\mathfrak m)=0$. So $\ker\phi=\mathfrak mA$; it is a proper ideal ($\phi(1)=1$), and every element outside it is a unit, so every proper ideal lies in it: $A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mA$. Also $\phi\circ\rho=\phi_{j_0}\rho_{j_0}=\varphi_0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 03C3, proof, third paragraph ('$R'=\colim_{i\in I}R_i$. This is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mR'$, and residue field $k'=\bigcup_{i\in I}k_i$'); the verification is written by the agent

proof.text: (Claim C, flatness.) In the situation of step 5, regard each $A_j$ as an $R$-module via $\rho_j$ and $A$ via $\rho$; the $\psi_{j'j}$ and $\iota_j$ are $R$-linear. We show that $(A,(\iota_j)_j)$ is a colimit of $(A_j,\psi_{j'j})$ in $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $g_j:A_j\to M$ be $R$-linear with $g_{j'}\psi_{j'j}=g_j$. Define $g(\iota_j(a))=g_j(a)$: every element of $A$ has this form [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise], and if $\iota_j(a)=\iota_{j'}(a')$ there is $j''\ge j,j'$ with $\psi_{j''j}(a)=\psi_{j''j'}(a')$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero], whence $g_j(a)=g_{j''}\psi_{j''j}(a)=g_{j''}\psi_{j''j'}(a')=g_{j'}(a')$; so $g$ is well defined, it is $R$-linear (compute at a common stage $j''$, where $\iota_{j''}$ is $R$-linear), $g\iota_j=g_j$, and it is unique since the $\iota_j$ jointly cover $A$. Every $A_j$ is a flat $R$-module ($\rho_j$ flat), so $A$ is a flat $R$-module [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-flat-modules], i.e. $\rho$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. With step 5, $(A,\rho,\phi)$ is an $R$-tower with image $\bigcup_j\phi_j(A_j)$, and $\iota_j:A_j\to A$ is compatible with the maps from $R$ and to $K$. This proves Claim C.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 03C3, proof, third paragraph ('the ring map $R\to R'$ is flat as it is a colimit of flat maps (and tensor products commute with directed colimits)')

proof.text: (The well-ordering and the subfields $K(x)$.) Choose a well-ordering $\le$ of the set $K$ [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem]. For $x\in K$ let $K(x)$ (resp. $K_{<x}$) be the subfield of $K$ generated by $F_0$ and $\{y\in K:y\le x\}$ (resp. $\{y:y<x\}$), i.e. the intersection of all subfields containing these. Then: (a) $K(x)=K_{<x}(x)$ [def-weil-simple-field-extension], both being the smallest subfield containing $F_0$, the $y<x$ and $x$; (b) $y\le x$ implies $K(y)\subseteq K(x)$, and $y<x$ implies $K(y)\subseteq K_{<x}$; (c) if $\{y<x\}=\emptyset$ then $K_{<x}=F_0$; if it is nonempty then $K_{<x}=\bigcup_{y<x}K(y)$: by (b) the $K(y)$, $y<x$, form a chain of subfields, so their union is a subfield, it contains $F_0$ and each $y<x$ ($y\in K(y)$), and it is contained in $K_{<x}$; (d) $\bigcup_{x\in K}K(x)=K$, as $z\in K(z)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 03C3, proof, fourth paragraph ('we choose a well ordering on $K$. For $x\in K$ we let $K(x)$ be the subfield of $K$ generated by all elements of $K$ which are $\leq x$')

proof.text: (The recursion.) For a subset $D\subseteq K$ closed downwards, a *coherent system on $D$* is a family of $R$-towers $(A_y,\rho_y,\phi_y)_{y\in D}$ with $\phi_y(A_y)=K(y)$ and ring maps $\psi_{y'y}:A_{y'}\to A_y$ for $y'\le y$ in $D$ satisfying the compatibilities of step 5 ($\psi_{yy}=\mathrm{id}$, $\psi_{y''y'}\psi_{y'y}=\psi_{y''y}$, $\psi_{y'y}\rho_{y'}=\rho_y$, $\phi_y\psi_{y'y}=\phi_{y'}$). Let $\mathcal V$ be the class of tuples $(A,\rho,\phi,(B_y,\beta_y)_{y\in K})$ with $A,B_y$ commutative rings and $\rho:R\to A$, $\phi:A\to K$, $\beta_y:B_y\to A$ ring maps. For $x\in K$ define $G_x$ on families $c=(c_y)_{y<x}$ in $\mathcal V$ as follows (fixing the choices once and for all by the axiom of choice). If $c$ is a coherent system on $\{y<x\}$ (the components of $c_y$ being $A_y,\rho_y,\phi_y$ and $\beta$'s from $A_{y'}$, $y'<y$, giving $\psi_{yy'}$): let $(A',\rho',\phi')=(R,\mathrm{id}_R,\varphi_0)$ if $\{y<x\}=\emptyset$ (an $R$-tower with image $F_0=K_{<x}$, step 7(c)); otherwise the colimit $R$-tower of Claim C (steps 5-6) over $J=\{y<x\}$, with image $\bigcup_{y<x}K(y)=K_{<x}$ (step 7(c)) and maps $\iota_y:A_y\to A'$. Apply step 4 to $(A',\rho',\phi')$ and $\alpha=x$: an $R$-tower $(A_x,\rho_x,\phi_x)$ with image $K_{<x}(x)=K(x)$ (step 7(a)) and $\beta:A'\to A_x$; put $G_x(c)=(A_x,\rho_x,\phi_x,(A_y,\beta\iota_y)_{y<x})$ (with $\psi_{xy}=\beta\iota_y$; no $\iota$'s in the empty case). If $c$ is not coherent, $G_x(c)=(R,\mathrm{id},\varphi_0,\emptyset)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] there is a family $(c_x)_{x\in K}$ with $c_x=G_x((c_y)_{y<x})$. By induction along the well-ordering (a least $x$ for which $(c_y)_{y\le x}$ fails to be coherent would have $(c_y)_{y<x}$ coherent: a failure of coherence on $\{y\le x'\}$ for some $x'<x$ would already occur below $x$), $(c_y)_{y\le x}$ is coherent for every $x$: if $(c_y)_{y<x}$ is coherent, $c_x$ is an $R$-tower with image $K(x)$ by construction, and the new maps satisfy the compatibilities: $\psi_{xy}\psi_{yy'}=\beta\iota_y\psi_{yy'}=\beta\iota_{y'}=\psi_{xy'}$, $\psi_{xy}\rho_y=\beta\iota_y\rho_y=\beta\rho'=\rho_x$, $\phi_x\psi_{xy}=\phi_x\beta\iota_y=\phi'\iota_y=\phi_y$ (steps 4, 6). Hence $(c_x)_{x\in K}$ is a coherent system on $K$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 03C3, proof, fourth paragraph ('By transfinite recursion on $x\in K$ we will produce ring maps $R\subset R(x)$ as in the lemma with residue field extension $K(x)/k$ ... $R(x)$ will contain $R(y)$ for all $y\leq x$'); the source treats successor and limit $x$ separately, here both by one rule (for $x$ with predecessor $x'$ the colimit over $\{y<x\}$ is $R(x')$ up to isomorphism), and the least element of $K$ is given $A'=R$ (the source's 'colimit over $x'<x$' would be over the empty set)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) $K$ is nonempty and totally ordered, so Claim C (steps 5-6) applies to the coherent system $(A_x,\rho_x,\phi_x,\psi_{xy})_{x\in K}$ of step 8: its colimit is an $R$-tower $(R',\varphi,\phi)$ with image $\bigcup_{x\in K}K(x)=K$ (step 7(d)). By step 1, $R'$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'=\mathfrak mR'$, $\varphi:R\to R'$ is flat and local, and $\phi$ induces an isomorphism $\kappa'=R'/\mathfrak m'\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ compatible with the maps from $\kappa$.
